titulo: KPIs, KQIs, QoS and QoE: from measurement to experience
resumo: The lecture closes the chain measurement, metric, KPI, KQI, QoS (SLA), QoE and decision. It starts with the sources (near-RT E2SM-KPM and management-side O1 PM) and with the anatomy of an indicator: name, formula, unit, granularity, source, threshold, window and interpretation. It then goes through the telecom KPI families and the UE channel indicators (RSRP, RSSI, RSRQ, SINR, CQI, MCS), shows how to compute accessibility, drop, availability, PRB utilization, throughput and delay, and writes the project formulas over the lab's three KPMs, including the KQI as a fraction above a threshold, the risk index and the anomaly rate. Next it separates QoS from QoE, places SLA, 5QI, QoS Flow and slice, and returns to the jammer case with the IQ watchdog and a spectral KPI to tell lack of capacity apart from interference. Everything converges on Checkpoint 2: at least two of the group's indicators defined and classified as KPI, KQI, QoS clause or QoE proxy.
objetivos: Walk the chain measurement, metric, KPI, KQI, QoS (SLA), QoE and decision, knowing that a KPM is not a KPI.
Write a complete indicator: name, formula, unit, granularity, source, target or threshold, window and interpretation.
Read the channel indicators (RSRP, RSSI, RSRQ, SINR, CQI, MCS) and the KPI families (accessibility, retainability, integrity, availability, utilization, mobility) to build testable hypotheses.
Compute the project KPIs per phase over RRU.PrbTotUl, DRB.UEThpUl and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, and turn delay into a KQI with a justified threshold.
Separate QoS from QoE, use SLA and 5QI as a reference and tell congestion apart from interference (jammer) by crossing KPM with a spectral KPI, in order to deliver Checkpoint 2.

conceitos.t: Indicator sources: E2SM-KPM, E2SM-RC and O1 PM
conceitos.d: E2SM-KPM (E2 Service Model for Key Performance Measurement) delivers standardized O-RAN measurements per UE and per cell, reported by the E2 node, with typical granularity from sub-second to seconds; it feeds near-RT KPIs in xApps and, once aggregated, non-RT analytics in rApps. E2SM-RC (RAN Control) closes the measurement-to-action loop over RRM (Radio Resource Management), and the E2 services (REPORT, INSERT, CONTROL, POLICY) have different granularity and delay. O1 PM (Performance Management) serves management and assurance in the SMO (Service Management and Orchestration): history, trends, NOC (Network Operations Center), data warehouse, with granularity aggregated in minutes. The two are not interchangeable channels: KPM has short retention at the edge and should not be dumped whole into BI. Every use case needs an explicit target KPI before any recommendation or A1 policy.

conceitos.t: The chain measurement, metric, KPI, KQI, decision
conceitos.d: A measurement or counter (KPM, PM) is the raw reported value: PRBs used, bytes, RLC delay. A metric is that value with explicit unit and aggregation (mean, p95). A KPI (Key Performance Indicator) is the performance indicator of the network, the infrastructure and operations; a KQI (Key Quality Indicator) is the service quality indicator, seen from the side of the service and the user; the decision is an operational recommendation or an A1 policy, simulated in the course. The lecture's rule is that a KPM is not a KPI: the KPM is the standardized measurement, the KPI is a derived indicator with formula, target and interpretation. In its complete version the chain continues into QoS (the KQI checked against the contract) and QoE (what the user feels) before the decision.

conceitos.t: KPI and KQI: network versus service
conceitos.d: A KPI measures network performance against an operational or contractual objective and answers whether the network is healthy, capable and available; RAN examples are PRB utilization, UL and DL throughput, cell availability, access success rate and drop rate. A KQI measures the quality of the delivered service and answers whether the service is good enough for the user or for the SLA; it is often composed of or derived from KPIs, such as the fraction of time with delay above a threshold. In the lab, mean UL PRB utilization is a KPI and the percentage of time with delay above the threshold is a KQI. KPIs typically come from aggregated O1 PM and E2 KPM and serve capacity, energy saving and RRM; KQIs combine KPIs, thresholds, application data and probes and serve SLA, prioritization and QoE. A good KPI does not guarantee a good KQI: with low PRB there can still be delay from a poor radio link, backhaul or core congestion.

An indicator only exists with a written formal definition: name, formula, unit, granularity, source, target or threshold, time window and interpretation. The lecture's example is mean UL PRB utilization: formula mean(RRU.PrbTotUl) per phase, unit in % of PRBs (or the count reported by the KPM), granularity of KPM sample aggregated by phase, source kpm.sqlite or JSONL in the RRU.PrbTotUl column, alert if the mean goes above 80, and interpretation as UL capacity pressure on the cell. Without one of these fields the number is neither comparable nor reproducible, and two analysts reach different values under the same name. This is exactly the contract Checkpoint 2 demands for each of the group's indicators.

conceitos.t: KPI families and the layers of the story
conceitos.d: The classic families are accessibility (success in establishing the service), retainability (drops after the session is established), integrity (quality of the data flow: throughput, BLER, loss, delay), availability (time on air), utilization (usage over capacity) and mobility (handover and reselection). The motivating case is the subscriber who, on a Friday at 7 pm, complains that video freezes: the symptom is QoE (buffering, low MOS, churn risk), MOS (Mean Opinion Score) being the average 1-to-5 rating given by users, and the operational question is whether the cause is coverage, interference, capacity, core or transport. To answer it, the lecture organizes KPIs in layers: coverage and channel (RSRP, RSRQ, SINR, CQI, MCS), capacity and load (PRB utilization, active UEs), integrity (throughput, latency, loss) and access, retention and mobility (CSSR, DCR, HOSR). The lecture's references are CSSR (Call/Session Setup Success Rate) above 98% good and below 95% bad, DCR (Drop Call Rate) below 1% good and above 2% bad, HOSR (Handover Success Rate) above 98% and below 95%, loss below 1% and above 2%, latency below 50 ms and above 100 ms, and PRB utilization below 60% and above 80%. Without well-defined indicators the team draws the cause out of a hat; with them the hypothesis becomes testable.

conceitos.t: UE channel indicators: RSRP, RSSI, RSRQ, SINR, CQI and MCS
conceitos.d: RSRP (Reference Signal Received Power) is the average power of the reference signal resource elements, in dBm; it answers whether the UE is covered (good above -95 dBm, bad below -110 dBm) and is not enough on its own for QoE. RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator) is the total received power, including interference and noise (good above -100 dBm, bad below -110 dBm), and RSRQ (Reference Signal Received Quality) relates the two over N resource blocks (good above -10 dB, bad below -15 dB), dropping when the cell is loaded or interference is strong. SINR (Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio) is a strong predictor of throughput and MCS (good above 20 dB, bad below 13 dB); high RSRP with low SINR points to interference or pilot pollution. The UE summarizes the channel in the CQI (Channel Quality Indicator, 0 to 15 in LTE), and the network picks the MCS (Modulation and Coding Scheme, from QPSK to 256-QAM with different code rates): good CQI and SINR allow more bits per symbol, a poor channel forces a conservative MCS to protect against BLER. The chain is channel, CQI, MCS and PRB, throughput and latency, and only then CSSR, DCR and HOSR and QoE; that is why the user in the elevator gets degraded video before the PRB KPI shows anything, and many PRBs with low MCS do not mean a good experience.

conceitos.t: What the lab actually measures, and in which unit
conceitos.d: The KPM artifact of the UE-TP lab carries three measurements: RRU.PrbTotUl (UL PRB occupancy, capacity layer, utilization and risk KPI), DRB.UEThpUl (UE UL throughput, integrity layer, throughput KPI) and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (downlink RLC delay, integrity and latency, KPI or KQI proxy). RSRP, RSRQ, CQI and MCS are not in the artifact and only come in as hypothesis context. The lecture's reading rule is: if throughput drops with high PRB, the hypothesis is capacity; if it drops with low PRB, think of the channel (SINR, MCS) or of core and transport. On units, slide 22 gives RRU.PrbTotUl in % of PRBs or count, slide 40 says it already arrives as a utilization of about 0 to 100, and slide 47 gives DRB.UEThpUl in the artifact's unit, usually kbps, to be converted if the report is in Mbps. For the delay, slides 43 and 48 use ms and slide 44 gives the example of delay above 150 ms, while the FlexRIC KPM xApp prints DRB.RlcSduDelayDl in µs (and so does slide 66 of lecture 01). The difference is a factor of a thousand and changes the threshold of a KQI, so the adopted unit must be declared in the README and checked against the xApp log.

conceitos.t: How to compute the KPIs and choose the aggregation
conceitos.d: Accessibility is successes over establishment attempts in the same window, with a target close to 100%; drop rate is abnormally terminated sessions over established sessions, and is not to be confused with accessibility because there the service had already started; availability is time on air (no outage, not locked) over the window, the basis of contracts and of outage alarms in the NOC. Setup counters are not in the UE-TP artifact, so these three stay as conceptual references. PRB utilization is PRBs used over PRBs available, and high utilization with falling throughput suggests congestion; throughput is bits transferred over the window duration, and p95 reads the value below which 95% of the samples lie; delay is summarized by mean, median or p95 and, with a threshold, becomes a KQI and QoE proxy. Aggregation changes the meaning: the mean is sensitive to outliers, the median is robust to spikes (useful with RFSIM), p95 and p99 show the tail the worst user feels, and the maximum is useful for capacity peaks but poor on its own as an SLA. The per-phase contrast baseline, stress and recovery is mandatory in CP2, and the README must state which aggregation was used and why.

conceitos.t: From threshold to KQI: the project formulas
conceitos.d: A formal KQI comes from a series and a threshold L: the fraction of samples in the phase or window with a value above L, for example the percentage of time with delay above the threshold. L must be justified by baseline statistics or by a service requirement, and without a documented L there is no KQI. The project KPIs are computed per phase: mean (or p95) of RRU.PrbTotUl, expecting stress far above baseline; median of DRB.UEThpUl, which resists RFSIM outliers, with optional p95 and the ratio median(stress)/median(baseline) declared in the README; and p95 of DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which uses the delay tail to approximate impact on the service and is combined with the fraction above L. The risk index is composite, marking 1 for a sample with PRB above Y and throughput below Z, with Y and Z justified by baseline or percentiles, and aggregated as a mean or percentage per phase. The anomaly rate is the percentage of anomalous samples per phase; the lab's MAD pipeline is a starting point, and false positives depend on the score threshold and on the minimum number of anomalous features.

conceitos.t: QoS and QoE, and the complete chain
conceitos.d: QoS (Quality of Service) is the quality of the service delivered by the network: objective, measurable and contractable in an SLA, such as latency below 50 ms, loss below 0.1% or a minimum throughput. QoE (Quality of Experience) is the quality perceived by the user: subjective or estimated, dependent on the application and context, expressed by voice or video MOS, by the complaint that it froze or by churn. The complete chain is measurement, KPI (resource and network), KQI (service quality), QoS (the KQI checked against SLA, 5QI or slice), QoE and decision. In the lab, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl with threshold L is a KQI and, if L is the SLA, a QoS check; but it is neither MOS nor an application score, it is a proxy for risk to the experience, and the project must state when QoE is only a proxy. The relationship is not linear: with a jammer the radio QoS degrades (SINR and throughput drop) and QoE falls even with PRBs to spare. In CP2 each indicator must be classified as KPI, KQI, QoS clause or QoE proxy.

An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is the service level agreement, with targets for availability, latency, throughput and others; a useful SLA states the indicator, the aggregation, the window and the fraction of time during which the target holds. The 5QI (5G QoS Identifier) defines the treatment class: GBR (Guaranteed Bit Rate) or non-GBR, priority and delay budget (PDB, Packet Delay Budget); per 3GPP TS 23.501, 5QI 1 is GBR voice with a 100 ms PDB and 5QI 9 is default non-GBR traffic with 300 ms. The QoS Flow is the unit of QoS in the 5GC and the RAN, grouping packets with the same treatment: the PDU session filters the packets, marks the QFI (QoS Flow Identifier), and the gNB multiplexes them into DRBs (Data Radio Bearers). A slice is a logical isolation with its own KPIs, KQIs and SLA; in slice SLA assurance the Near-RT RIC optimizes E2 actions to keep the targets, and the SMO correlates O1 PM, A1 policies and O2 events per NSSI (Network Slice Subnet Instance). The lab's KPM artifact has no real 5QI, so thresholds come in as didactic SLA clauses, and the alarm threshold must state whether it is statistical or contractual and what the detection delay is.

Each service class is sensitive to a different QoS: eMBB and download depend on throughput (symptom: slow, endless download; lab proxy: UE throughput), video streaming depends on stable throughput and jitter (buffering and lower resolution; proxy: delay p95 and fraction above L), voice and conferencing depend on latency and loss (echo, cuts, low MOS; delay is a weak proxy), and URLLC depends on extreme latency and reliability, outside the RFSIM scope. Metrics lead to typical decisions: throughput (RAN KPM, core, app) to capacity and steering; latency and jitter (RLC, x-haul, UDP/TCP) to prioritization and fronthaul upgrade; loss (link, queue, radio) to retransmission and coverage; availability and utilization (cell, link) to maintenance and energy saving. Indicators also live in different domains: RAN (PRB, RLC delay, UE throughput), core (session success, drop rate), transport (fronthaul latency and loss, link utilization, path QoS) and terminal or application (UE RSRP, MOS, video stalls, with ethical care). An application's QoE usually combines several of these metrics, and a drop in a radio KPI can be a symptom of queuing in transport or in the core.

conceitos.t: IQ watchdog, spectral KPI and the jammer case
conceitos.d: The IQ watchdog is one more source, from the RF domain, next to the E2 KPM: it sees energy on the air in time and frequency, answers whether there is interference and usually sees the cause in the PHY first, while KPM and PM see the effect on the service later. In the lab captures (fs = 200e6, fc = 3.75e9, 20 s), OFDM traffic shows up as horizontal blocks of about 100 MHz, and the jammer on the SSB (Synchronization Signal Block) as a continuous narrow stain; .npy spectrograms and PSD are bronze, alerts are gold. The pipeline is IQ, windowed FFT, PSD and spectrogram (silver), threshold, score or ML up to the spectral KPI (gold), and a temporal join in UTC with the KPM throughput, PRB and delay. Possible spectral KPIs: anomalous occupancy (% of bins with PSD above baseline plus k times MAD), energy in the SSB region, interference score, anomaly duty (fraction of time with score above L, a KQI) and jammer class. The didactic hypothesis: load raises PRB and throughput together (capacity), whereas with a jammer the spectral score rises and then throughput drops or delay rises without classic PRB saturation; the decision is to investigate RF, WIPS (Wireless Intrusion Prevention System) or a candidate A1 policy in dry-run, not simply to add more PRBs. Access counters such as CSSR do not come out of IQ, because IQ shows energy, not sessions.

conceitos.t: Checkpoint 2, bridge to optimization and synthesis
conceitos.d: Checkpoint 2 (20 min) asks for at least two indicators, each with name, formula, unit, granularity, source (artifact and metric), interpretation and validity limit, classified without mixing as KPI, KQI, QoS clause (SLA) or QoE proxy, with one initial chart per KPI carrying title, axes and time window, and a discussion of which decision the indicator enables and whether the threshold is a didactic SLA. In the bridge to lecture 05, QoE optimization starts from requirements that vary per application and over the session, estimates QoE from QoS metrics plus context, and acts through Non-RT RIC A1 policies and E2SM-KPM and RC in the Near-RT RIC; in the project the group optimizes the KQI or SLA it defined, without claiming application QoE without evidence. The video QoE case study in Open RAN asks what goes to near-RT and to non-RT, what stays in the lake and in the warehouse, how to tell radio congestion from UPF congestion, and what the privacy risks are when estimating QoE per UE. The synthesis: define the indicator before optimizing or automating, KPI is not KQI, which is not QoS, which is not QoE, and an A1 policy does not fix a badly defined indicator.

formulas.expr: RSRQ = N * RSRP / RSSI (lineares; em dB: RSRQ = 10*log10(N) + RSRP_dBm - RSSI_dBm); SINR = P_signal / (P_interference + P_noise)
formulas.vars: N number of resource blocks in the measurement; RSRP reference signal power; RSSI total received power including interference and noise; P_signal, P_interference, P_noise powers of the useful signal, interference and noise
formulas.quando: Channel diagnosis: RSRQ good above -10 dB and bad below -15 dB; SINR good above 20 dB, acceptable between 13 and 20 dB and bad below 13 dB

formulas.vars: N_success attempts that completed establishment (RRC setup or session); N_attempts total attempts in the same window
formulas.quando: Access KPI with a target close to 100% (CSSR good above 98%); setup counters are not in the UE-TP artifact, it is a reference concept

formulas.vars: N_drops abnormally terminated sessions; N_sessions sessions established in the window
formulas.quando: Retention: the lower the better (DCR good below 1%, bad above 2%); the service had already started, unlike accessibility

formulas.vars: T_available time on air, without outage or locked state; T_total duration of the observation window, in the same time zone and unit
formulas.quando: Availability contracts and outage alarms in the NOC; in the lab the cell is usually always up, so it is a conceptual reference

formulas.vars: PRB_used blocks allocated in the period; PRB_available carrier total (e.g. 106 PRB in 40 MHz with 30 kHz SCS)
formulas.quando: Capacity pressure; RRU.PrbTotUl already arrives as utilization (about 0 to 100); high utilization with falling throughput suggests congestion

formulas.expr: Thp = soma(bits transferidos) / Δt; Thp_p95 = P95({Thp_1, Thp_2, ..., Thp_N})
formulas.vars: Δt window duration, the same interval as the counter; Thp_i throughput of each sample (DRB.UEThpUl is already throughput per sample); N samples
formulas.unidade: Mbps in operations; kbps in the KPM artifact
formulas.quando: Mean or median for the typical case; p95 for the near-worst case, bad-user SLA and baseline x stress contrast

formulas.vars: d_i delay of sample i (in the lab, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, downlink RLC delay); N samples in the window
formulas.unidade: the artifact's unit: the slide uses ms, the FlexRIC xApp prints µs
formulas.quando: Integrity KPI; the median is robust, p95 emphasizes the tail; with a threshold it becomes a KQI and QoE proxy

formulas.vars: d_i samples of the series (delay or another metric); L threshold justified by baseline statistics or a service requirement; N samples in the phase or window
formulas.quando: Turn a series into a service quality indicator; without a documented L there is no formal KQI; if L is the SLA, it is a QoS check

formulas.expr: KPI_PRB(p) = mean(RRU.PrbTotUl | phase = p); KPI_Thp(p) = median(DRB.UEThpUl | phase = p); KPI_Delay(p) = P95(DRB.RlcSduDelayDl | phase = p); razao = median(Thp | stress) / median(Thp | baseline)
formulas.vars: p ∈ {baseline, stress, recovery}; optional: P95 instead of the PRB mean, and throughput P95
formulas.unidade: PRB in %; throughput in the artifact's unit (usually kbps); delay in the declared unit (slide 48: ms; xApp log: µs); ratio dimensionless
formulas.quando: Checkpoint 2: stress far above baseline in PRB is the expected contrast in UE-TP; declare the ratio and the units in the README

formulas.expr: Risco_i = 1 se PRB_i > Y e Thp_i < Z; 0 caso contrário; KPI = média(Risco) ou % de amostras com Risco = 1, por fase
formulas.vars: PRB_i and Thp_i utilization and throughput of sample i; Y and Z thresholds justified by baseline or percentiles
formulas.unidade: dimensionless (0 or 1); aggregated as a fraction or %
formulas.quando: Composite indicator combining PRB pressure with throughput degradation

formulas.vars: N_anomalas samples classified as anomalous in the phase (e.g. the lab's MAD pipeline); N_amostras samples in the phase
formulas.quando: Per phase (baseline vs stress); discuss false positives through the score threshold and the minimum number of anomalous features

formulas.expr: S_t = (PSD_t^peak - mediana(PSD_t)) / (MAD(PSD_baseline) + ε); KQI_L = #{t : S_t > L} / N * 100%
formulas.vars: PSD_t^peak peak of the spectral density in window t; mediana(PSD_t) typical level of the window; MAD(PSD_baseline) robust spread of the jammer-free baseline; ε avoids division by zero; L threshold (e.g. 3); N windows
formulas.unidade: S_t dimensionless; KQI in % of time (anomaly duty)
formulas.quando: IQ watchdog: high S_t means a peak outside clean behavior; cross it in time with throughput, PRB and delay to separate jammer from capacity

onde.texto: In P2 the three KPMs are born in the OAI gNB (E2SM-KPM), go through FlexRIC and the xApp and become a file. p2-kpi-qoe walks this lecture's chain over that telemetry (KPM measurement, KPI, KQI, QoS with a didactic SLA, QoE as a proxy and decision) and ends with the anatomy of the Checkpoint 2 indicators; p2-tema-t1 to t7 compute each theme's KPIs per phase, with the formula printed before the number.

quiz.q: In the stress phase UE throughput drops, RRU.PrbTotUl is close to 99% and RLC delay rises. The artifact has no RSRP or CQI. Is this a QoS violation or resource saturation, and how would you formalize it?
quiz.a: By the lecture's rule, throughput dropping with high PRB points to capacity: it is resource saturation, observed through KPIs (mean or p95 PRB utilization per phase, median throughput). It only becomes a QoS matter when a KQI is checked against a contract threshold: for example KQI_L = percentage of samples with DRB.RlcSduDelayDl above L, with L declared as a didactic SLA and in the unit checked in the xApp log. Without RSRP, SINR or CQI a poor channel cannot be ruled out, and without MOS nothing can be claimed about QoE; in a real network you would ask for that UE and cell data.

quiz.q: A phase has 60 DRB.RlcSduDelayDl samples, and 18 of them are above threshold L. Compute the KQI and say what is missing for it to be valid in Checkpoint 2.
quiz.a: KQI_L = 18 / 60 * 100% = 30% of samples above L. To be valid in CP2 it still needs: a justification for L (baseline statistics or a service requirement), the declared unit of the delay and the threshold (the slides use ms, the FlexRIC xApp prints µs, and a factor of a thousand changes everything), the granularity (per phase) and the source (artifact column), and a classification: it is a KQI and, if L is treated as an SLA, a QoS clause; never measured QoE.

quiz.q: The watchdog's spectral score S_t goes above 3 and, shortly after, UE throughput drops with stable PRB and no saturation. What is the preferred hypothesis and what decision makes sense?
quiz.a: RF interference or a jammer, not lack of capacity: under load, PRB and throughput rise together; with a jammer, anomalous energy appears first in the spectrum (cause in the PHY) and the effect comes later in the KPM (throughput drops, delay rises) without saturated PRB. It is confirmed with a temporal join in UTC between S_t and the KPM and with the anomaly duty. The decision is to investigate RF and trigger WIPS or a candidate A1 policy in dry-run, not to add PRBs, which would not address the cause.
